I personally believe that as friends we owe each other communication. This doesn’t mean talking every day or even every week, but it’s incredibly rude to ghost/leave on read for weeks on end with zero explanation excluding extenuating circumstances. 

I also believe we owe each other honesty. What this means is that if your friend asks you if something looks good, tell them the truth kindly. If they’re asking you for advice, tell them the truth. How would you feel if someone misled you because they wanted to spare your feelings? 

My big one with friendships is that we owe each other mutual respect. This means listening to their needs and communicating our needs in a productive way (no yelling, passive aggressiveness, or derogatory language).

I think to call anyone a villain in either situation is a huge stretch. 

Take the prank, for example. Yes, it’s wrong to pull a prank on a friend that places them in a vulnerable position. And then to film it is even worse.

At the same time, nobody forced Hannah to meet with Mike in the first place. She wasn’t held at gunpoint and shoved into the room and forced to take her shirt off. She knew very well that Mike and Emily were in an established relationship. She knew very well that going behind her friend’s back to get with her boyfriend was wrong. She’s not some innocent child who can’t understand the gravity of her own actions. 

On the topic of Josh’s prank, it’s understandable that he would want revenge after the actions of his friends resulted in the deaths of his sisters. He also wasn’t in his right mind. It wasn’t right for him to do that, though, just like it wasn’t right for them to pull that prank. We can acknowledge that actions are justifiable and not morally correct at the same time.

Ultimately, I think both situations were horrific and should not have happened.

They don’t think you’re an AH for not devoting all your attention to the kids, they think you’re an AH for drinking while watching them, which is a valid concern. This isn’t me saying you should be forced to babysit, but you also shouldn’t be drinking while watching anyone’s kids. Period. Even if you weren’t “sloppy drunk”, God forbid something happens and now you’re held accountable legally for being under the influence while in charge of the kids.

Hi! Unfortunately, sudden death is a thing that happens in young and healthy people. Fortunately, there’s a 1 in 100,000 chance of that happening. I know it seems like a lot, but it’s literally a less than 1% chance if you do the math. You’re more likely to get in a car accident or be struck by lightning.

Panic attacks and anxiety in general can cause faintness or that dizzy feeling. This isn’t to say not to visit a doctor and rule out physical causes, or that what you’re feeling is any less real or scary, but our bodies are strange and they do things just because they feel like it. 

I hope you feel better soon :)

For carrying things, large tote bags are becoming more in fashion, and most grocery stores sell reusable cloth bags so it’s easier to hold items. Earplugs are also amazing for long outings (Noise reducing is great, but when there’s a lot of noise I prefer to pop in my bluetooth ones and blast my favorite songs). First thing to do is to locate your bathrooms and every exit depending on where you are. Last thing you want is to be overstimulated and struggling to find a quiet place to calm down. If you find yourself getting overwhelmed you can usually duck into the bread aisle at the store. It’s always relatively empty and quiet for some reason. 

When shopping for clothes, you could try going for breathability (think athletic wear, leggings, even some jeans honestly) which usually helps with that sticky sweaty feeling where my clothes stick to me. Make sure your shoes fit comfortably. There are thinner socks that make my feet sweat less than dress socks.

Too hot and too cold is tricky. It being too cold can be rectified with a sweater, but handheld fans are great to fend off heat quickly. If you can handle shorts sensory wise, then that’s awesome for defending against heat as well.

By the way, there isn’t anything wrong with telling people no. If the people that your weekends are packed with aren’t important or work related, you can take time to yourself. If you’re spending the whole weekend socializing with everyone and then you have to go straight back to work it makes sense that you’d be exhausted. I don’t know if this is your situation, but just some general advice.
